findings.issue_text: [Critical/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:72 — `organization_context` is referenced (`organization_context.member.has_global_access`) but never defined, imported, or added by this diff; the `enable_advanced = ...` assignment runs unconditionally on every GET, so every audit-logs request from a non-superuser raises `NameError` → 500 (complete endpoint outage). Even if the variable existed, `.member` can be `None` and would raise `AttributeError`.

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:~819 — `OptimizedCursorPaginator` subclasses `BasePaginator` but never implements `build_queryset` (abstract on `BasePaginator` → `NotImplementedError`) and calls `self._is_asc` / `self.desc`, which are defined only on `CursorPaginator`/`DateTimePaginator` → `AttributeError`; the paginator can never return a page and should subclass `CursorPaginator`/`DateTimePaginator` rather than paste a copy of `get_result`.

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:~826 (`OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key`) — applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the row attribute, but the endpoint uses `order_by="-datetime"` so the value is a `datetime` and key/cursor generation raises `TypeError`; this was copied from the numeric-key `CursorPaginator`, while `DateTimePaginator` overrides it to use `.timestamp()`.

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:~830 (`OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor`) — returns the raw cursor integer instead of converting the unix timestamp back to a datetime (as `DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor` does), so `build_queryset` filters a `DateTimeField` against an int → DB error or broken filtering on every page after the first.

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:~878-884 (negative-offset branch) — `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start raises Django's `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`, so the "advanced" path 500s whenever triggered; the comment claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false, and even list-style negative slicing would return the tail of the queryset, not "data beyond normal pagination bounds".

[Medium/api] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-183 — unrequested behavior change in a shared paginator used by many endpoints: forward cursors with negative offsets now silently clamp to offset 0 (previously a 500), masking malformed cursors, while prev cursors with negative offsets still raise `AssertionError`; only one of the duplicated `get_result` implementations in this file is patched, making malformed-cursor handling inconsistent across paginator classes, and the "queryset will handle boundary conditions" comment is false.

[Medium/test_gap] No tests are added for `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, the negative-offset branches, or the modified shared `get_result`; the shared change affects every endpoint using this paginator class, and any test exercising the new endpoint path would have immediately caught the `NameError`/`NotImplementedError`.

[Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820-827 & src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27 — docstrings/comments advertise capabilities that don't exist ("optimized query path for large datasets", "efficient bidirectional pagination without full dataset scanning", "efficient reverse pagination"); the new class performs identical query/slicing work to `CursorPaginator`, and the cursors.py change is comment-only, endorsing the broken negative-offset design for future maintainers.

[Low/api] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — introduces an undocumented, client-controlled `optimized_pagination` query param that switches paginator/cursor semantics with no feature flag or rollout control, and which is silently ignored (falling back to the old paginator) for non-admin users.

Even if the variable existed, `.member` can be `None` and would raise `AttributeError`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` in `organization_auditlogs.py` without showing any definition/import of `organization_context` in this change. That reference is evaluated on every request (for non-superusers, the RHS is evaluated due to `or` short-circuit rules), so if `organization_context` is not defined in the surrounding function/module, it will raise `NameError` and 500 the endpoint. Additionally, the expression assumes `organization_context.member` is non-null, which could raise `AttributeError` if `member` can be `None`.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is introduced as `class OptimizedCursorPaginator(BasePaginator)` but it does not define several methods/attrs it immediately relies on: `self.build_queryset(...)` in `get_result`, and `self._is_asc(...)` / `self.desc` / `self.key` in `get_item_key`. Unless `BasePaginator` provides all of these (not shown in the diff), this will raise runtime errors (`AttributeError` / potentially `NotImplementedError`) when the new paginator is selected in `organization_auditlogs.py`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:~830 (`OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor`) — returns the raw cursor integer instead of converting the unix timestamp back to a datetime (as `DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor` does), so `build_queryset` filters a `DateTimeField` against an int → DB error or broken filtering on every page after the first.

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is used by `organization_auditlogs.py` with `order_by="-datetime"`, i.e. against a `DateTimeField`. But `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor` just returns `cursor.value` unchanged, and `get_item_key` assumes the field value is numeric (`math.floor/ceil(value)` then `int(...)`). There’s no conversion to/from `datetime` like a `DateTimePaginator` would need, so cursor values and queryset filtering/key extraction will be the wrong type for a datetime-ordered queryset (likely causing type errors or broken filtering once a nonzero cursor is used).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-183 — unrequested behavior change in a shared paginator used by many endpoints: forward cursors with negative offsets now silently clamp to offset 0 (previously a 500), masking malformed cursors, while prev cursors with negative offsets still raise `AssertionError`; only one of the duplicated `get_result` implementations in this file is patched, making malformed-cursor handling inconsistent across paginator classes, and the "queryset will handle boundary conditions" comment is false.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes shared pagination semantics in `paginator.py` by clamping forward (non-`is_prev`) negative offsets to 0 (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`), while leaving `is_prev` negative offsets untouched, which will still hit Django queryset negative slicing and raise (likely `AssertionError`). Additionally, the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` explicitly allows negative slicing when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, with comments claiming the ORM “properly handles negative slicing,” but Django querysets do not support negative slicing—so this path can 500 on crafted/malformed cursors. Only the earlier `get_result` is patched; other paginator implementations in the same file remain behaviorally different, making malformed-cursor handling inconsistent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] No tests are added for `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, the negative-offset branches, or the modified shared `get_result`; the shared change affects every endpoint using this paginator class, and any test exercising the new endpoint path would have immediately caught the `NameError`/`NotImplementedError`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new pagination behavior (new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with an `enable_advanced_features` negative-offset path) and also modifies shared paginator slicing logic in `sentry/api/paginator.py:get_result` (introducing `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). No tests are added anywhere in this diff to cover the new class or the new/changed branches, despite the shared `get_result` change potentially impacting all endpoints using that paginator. The finding’s specific references to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and the negative-offset branches are grounded in the added/modified code, though the mention of a specific `NameError`/`NotImplementedError` is not directly verifiable from the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820-827 & src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27 — docstrings/comments advertise capabilities that don't exist ("optimized query path for large datasets", "efficient bidirectional pagination without full dataset scanning", "efficient reverse pagination"); the new class performs identical query/slicing work to `CursorPaginator`, and the cursors.py change is comment-only, endorsing the broken negative-offset design for future maintainers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds extensive comments/docstrings claiming “optimized query path”, “efficient bidirectional pagination without full dataset scanning”, and “efficient reverse pagination” (e.g., new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` docstring and comments in `Cursor.get_result` / `Cursor.__init__`), but the shown implementation largely does the same queryset slicing pattern (`results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`) with only minor offset handling, and `cursors.py` change is comment-only. From the diff alone, these performance claims are not substantiated by any concrete optimization beyond slicing, so the finding about misleading documentation is diff-grounded (even if exact equivalence to `CursorPaginator` can’t be fully proven without its full code).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — introduces an undocumented, client-controlled `optimized_pagination` query param that switches paginator/cursor semantics with no feature flag or rollout control, and which is silently ignored (falling back to the old paginator) for non-admin users.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new client-controlled query param `optimized_pagination` (organization_auditlogs.py: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) that switches from `DateTimePaginator` to a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with different cursor behavior. This is gated only by `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` and otherwise silently falls back to the old paginator. There is no feature-flag/rollout control shown in the diff, so the concern about introducing an opt-in semantic switch via a query param without rollout control is grounded; however, it's more of an API/architecture/release-management issue than a concrete correctness defect. The claim that it's "undocumented" cannot be verified from the diff alone.
